subject: Vendr onboarding: ephemeral upload + presign edge cases
messages:
From: Elaine Morris <elaine@starlight.ai>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@starlight.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Vendr onboarding kick-off: ephemeral uploads and presign windows

Hi Ro han / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're kicking off Vendr profile claim for Starlight and have a couple of non-standard asks on the upload flow that I wanted to surface before the onboarding call:

- We need a short-lived, presign-based upload workflow where our users upload zipped evidence packages to your S3 bucket via presigned PUTs (TTL ~6 hours).
- For automation reasons we also need an "ephemeral service account" option used only for bulk ingest windows (scoped to a single bucket/prefix + PutObject).
- We have a SOC 2 excerpt requirement: a redacted control statement for the evidence that references KMS envelope encryption and access logs. Can Redwood provide the control excerpt or a pointer to the SOC doc we should reference?

I've attached a short presign policy doc (starlight-presign-policy.docx) and included our Vendr claim link: https://vendr.starlight.ai/profile/claim/3452.

Can you confirm the recommended pattern for temporary creds vs Vendr-managed presign role and any known edge cases (multi-part uploads, large zip chunking)? If helpful we can do a 20-minute screen share later this week.

Thanks,
Elaine Morris
Head of Security Operations
Starlight AI

--
Attachment: starlight-presign-policy.docx (docx)

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendr onboarding kick-off: ephemeral uploads and presign windows

Hi Elaine — thanks for the summary and the Vendr claim link. Looping in Kar thik (portal/onboarding) and Mina (security evidence) to confirm the recommended pattern. A few clarifying questions so we scope the right approach:

1) Scope: Are these uploads intended for a staging-only window initially, or will you go straight to production buckets? That affects retention and TTL defaults.
2) Multipart uploads: do you expect parallel multipart PUTs? Our presign flow supports S3 multipart but there are extra checks for manifest reassembly.
3) Least-privilege: do you prefer Redwood to create a short-lived role (assume-role -> presign) or receive a short-lived service account/key from your side that we accept for a narrow window?

Preliminary guidance: for bulk evidence we usually recommend Vendr-managed presigns (Redwood issues presigned URLs from an internal service role) and a one-off scoped upload window. That avoids sharing long-lived keys. If you need a service account for automation, we can create one with explicit PutObject on the prefix and a TTL of X hours — but that is an exception and requires SOC audit notes.

Proposed next steps:
- Kar thik / Mina and I will run a quick internal checklist (manifest schema, max object size, bucket prefix policy).
- Can we book 30 minutes Thu 08/06 10:00–10:30 PT to walk through the manifest and presign behavior? I sent a tentative invite (if this time doesn't work, propose alternatives).

I'll attach our SOC2 controls excerpt for the parts customers commonly ask about.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@starlight.ai
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendr onboarding kick-off: ephemeral uploads and presign windows

Thanks Rohan — good questions. Some specifics from our side:

- We'll do an initial staging window for the first week, then cut over to production. For the staging window we want presign TTL=6 hours. For production we can drop to 2 hours.
- Multipart: yes, our packager does parallel multipart uploads for large bundles (~1–2GB). If Redwood presigns multipart, we just need the canonical ETag behavior documented so Vendr can validate reassembly.
- Ephemeral service account: we prefer Redwood to issue a short-lived role we can assume (STS AssumeRole) for automated pulls from our side; that role must be limited to a single prefix + PutObject and have no List/Delete.

Soc2 ask: we need a short text snippet confirming that uploaded evidence is encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS (or Redwood KMS) and that object-level access and Put/Delete events are logged to an immutable audit trail for the retention window. If you can point to a published excerpt (or attach), that would be perfect — procurement needs it for the contract.

I attached a one-page presign FAQ and the Vendr claim in case you need it.

Elaine

--
Attachment: starlight-presign-policy.docx

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendr onboarding kick-off: ephemeral uploads and presign windows

Elaine — thanks for the clarifications; that's helpful. Summary and next steps below.

Summary:
- Staging window first (presign TTL=6h), production cutover with TTL=2h.
- Redwood will issue a scoped AssumeRole for automated workflows; role will have sts:AssumeRole and PutObject rights scoped to the agreed prefix. No List/Delete.
- Multipart uploads supported via presigned multipart flow; we'll share canonical ETag reassembly notes and a small manifest schema.
- SOC2 excerpt: attached redwood-soc2-controls-excerpt.pdf. It includes the KMS encryption and object-level logging verbiage we usually provide for vendor portals. If you need a signed attestation we can route via Legal/Compliance.

Action items I own:
1) Create the onboarding manifest template + example (will post to the Vendr claim and to the SharePoint link).
2) Provision a one-time AssumeRole for your staging window; you'll assume it with STS for automation. I will include the exact ARN and the expiration policy in the secure instructions file.
3) Share presign multipart ETag handling doc (small checklist).

Attachments: redwood-soc2-controls-excerpt.pdf, temporary-creds-instructions.txt

Proposed call: Thu 08/06 10:00–10:30 PT (I left the tentative invite). Please confirm and we'll lock the time.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
